narrative:
The RaMP enrichment analysis identified **Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG map00260)** as the top pathway (FDR=0.0, fold-enrichment=568.9), with six matched input metabolites. A second major hit was **Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives (Reactome R-HSA-71291)**, also significant. Key driver compounds in the amino-acid metabolism cluster include ornithine (C00077), L-methionine (C00073), S-adenosylhomocysteine (C00021), L-cysteine (C00097), and 2-ketobutyric acid (C00109); all were confirmed present in these pathways via membership lookups. (R)-Lipoic acid (C16241), an essential cofactor in the same metabolic sphere, also maps to this network.

Directional analysis confirmed that **L-methionine is upstream of S-adenosylhomocysteine** via the methionine cycle (path: C00073 → C00019 → C00021, length=2 hops), establishing a clear one-carbon donor relationship. Perturbations in this cycle affect methyl-donor availability systemically. The concurrent elevation of ornithine and cysteine suggests altered polyamine biosynthesis and sulfur amino-acid trafficking, both tightly linked to the methionine–homocysteine hub. Elevated 5,6-dihydroxyindole (C05578) may reflect downstream effects on melanin or catecholamine pathways. Finally, nitrate (C00244) elevation is consistent with inflammatory or oxidative-stress-driven nitrogen-oxide metabolism.

Collectively, these changes point to a treatment-induced rewiring of amino-acid and one-carbon metabolism, centred on the methionine–homocysteine cycle and its connected cysteine and polyamine branches, with systemic implications for methylation capacity and oxidative balance.
